items.title: US to build two military bases in Greenland under new deal with Denmark
items.description: The defence deal signed at the UN General Assembly also re-affirms Denmark's sovereignty over its semi-autonomous Arctic territory.

items.title: How Ceuta, football and Israel are shaping Morocco's election
items.description: Young voters are being courted with football slogans, promises of jobs and anti-Israel rallying calls.

items.title: Sri Lanka court convicts 15 men over deadly Easter Sunday bombings
items.description: Three churches and three luxury hotels were targeted in the 2019 attacks which killed 270.

items.title: Developing El Niño becomes strongest on record weeks before expected peak
items.description: Scientists say the developing El Niño is now the strongest on record with weather impacts already being felt around the world.

items.title: Ukraine anger as EU removes Russian oligarchs from sanctions list
items.description: Alisher Usmanov and Mikhail Fridman both have close ties to President Putin, and Kyiv said the move sent Moscow the wrong signals.

items.title: Lindsay Clancy's lawyer asks judge to investigate juror and check his phone
items.description: The attorney wants the court to look at the juror's mobile phone use and answers on questionnaires.

items.title: Eleven injured in shooting outside Turkish school
items.description: Footage appears to show a male in the area carrying a firearm, while officials say the attacker has been captured.

items.title: Top South African policeman charged with sexual offences
items.description: Shadrack Sibiya, who has made no comment, is alleged to have groomed a 16-year-old and raped an 18-year-old.

items.title: Autopsy shows Hayden Panettiere died from a drug overdose
items.description: The death of the child star - who had fentanyl, Xanax, a muscle relaxant and antipsychotic medication in her system - was ruled an accident.

items.title: Cyclist who dressed as man to avoid Taliban wins silver medal
items.description: Afghan cyclist Fariba Hashimi wins silver in the women's road race at the Asian Games, having fled oppression in her home country to pursue a sporting dream.

items.title: Veteran BBC Africa correspondent Mark Doyle dies aged 67
items.description: Doyle was best known for reporting on African conflicts in the 1990s and 2000s, notably in Rwanda and Sierra Leone.

items.title: Iran must stop arming Houthis in Yemen, G7 says ahead of UN General Assembly
items.description: The G7 also condemns "in the strongest terms" Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia, saying that the escalation in fighting in Yemen jeopardises global energy security.

items.title: Four dead after powerful Typhoon Dujuan lashes Japan
items.description: The storm pulled away from Japan after bringing heavy rains and strong winds to Tokyo and surrounding areas.

items.title: Lithuania ready to 'fight back' but has evacuation plans in face of Russia threats, PM tells BBC
items.description: Sinkevičius told BBC Newsnight Lithuanians feel "constantly threatened" by Moscow, but the nation was prepared to "fight back" if attacked.

items.title: 'I have never felt heat like that' - a survivor on watching 33 cellmates die in Nigeria
items.description: The BBC goes inside the prison where prisoners were trapped in stifling, cramped conditions.

items.title: Neutral venues and no 'away' fans - how Israel v Republic of Ireland became so contentious
items.description: BBC Sport explores the backdrop to the Republic of Ireland's matches against Israel, amid fraught tensions between the nations.

items.title: What is the White House pool and why is it in a row with Trump?
items.description: The White House press pool is at the centre of a major row between President Donald Trump and TV networks. What is it?

items.title: Why a Bollywood celebrity manager's 2020 death case has been reopened
items.description: Disha Salian's father insists her death was not suicide or an accident, but that she was gang-raped and murdered.

items.title: Why is the Bab al-Mandab Strait so important?
items.description: The BBC's Frank Gardner explains why the narrow waterway is key to oil transportation and the world economy.

items.title: What to expect as world leaders descend on New York - and who won't be there
items.description: The BBC’s Sarah Smith outlines which world leaders Trump is set to meet and the key topics expected on the agenda.
